answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity's actions are hashed into a rolling kernel per epoch; a new epoch only admits identities whose kernel overlaps the prior epoch's more than a threshold. Sybil clusters register cheaply but cannot fake sustained history, since every extra identity must maintain distinct, stable behaviour across epochs. The per-identity cost is continuous activity and record-keeping—like tending a saffron crop—plus a growing nebula of archived proofs an attacker must store and replay consistently.
